title: Samsung's Q3 profit seen jumping nine-fold, but chip margins may be flat
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Samsung Electronics is expected to deliver a nearly ninefold increase in third-quarter operating profit, as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure continues to support memory chip sales. However, forecasts suggest its memory business may struggle to expand profitability further.

According to Reuters, the LSEG SmartEstimate puts operating profit at 106.1 trillion won, compared with 12.17 trillion won a year earlier. The estimate, drawn from 21 analysts, has fallen 7.7% since late August as memory price increases moderate and the South Korean won strengthens.

SK Securities analyst Han Dong-hee expects Samsung’s memory chip operating margin to reach 76%, unchanged from the previous quarter. TrendForce forecasts conventional DRAM contract prices will increase 10% to 15% in the fourth quarter, considerably slower than the roughly 60% increase recorded in the second quarter.

Samsung also has an opportunity in high-bandwidth memory, which supports AI processors. J.P. Morgan estimates its HBM market share could rise to 34% this year from 20% last year. Preliminary quarterly results are due October 8, with detailed figures following this month.

The contrast between surging profit and flat margins reflects two different comparisons. The profit forecast measures improvement against last year, while the margin estimate compares profitability with the immediately preceding quarter. Both can therefore be true without contradiction.

For investors, the distinction raises a question about what drives the next phase of growth. If margins stop widening, further earnings gains may depend more heavily on sales volume and the mix of products Samsung sells. Strong demand alone does not guarantee continuing improvements in profit earned per unit of revenue.

The forthcoming results will help show whether Samsung can sustain momentum as pricing gains slow. Its progress in HBM could become particularly important, giving the company another route to growth while customers and competitors adjust to an unusually profitable memory market.
